# mosh / terminal_fuzzer

mosh's own fuzz target `terminal_fuzzer` ([source](source/terminal_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over mosh (mobile-shell/mosh at decd9b70).

Feeds every input byte as a UserByte to an 80x24 Terminal::Complete, then renders a frame diff (Display::new_frame) against a blank framebuffer; output string discarded.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against mosh at commit decd9b70.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch mosh` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libncursesw.a` (a library from the build image), `libprotobuf.a` (a library from the build image), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
